name: Calculating the Employee's Wage Based on the Hours That the Employee Has Worked and an Hourly Pay Rate
description: Construct a program for the payment department of a company to calculate the wage of an employee based on the number of hours that the employee has worked. If an employee works over 40 hours in a week, the payment amount should take into account the overtime hours. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate.

comments.content: The constant RATE is the regular hourly pay rate.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.
The constant STANDARD is the standard hours in a work week.

Note that constants hold a particular value for the duration of their existence and their value cannot be changed after initialization. By convention, uppercase letters are used when naming constants.
The variable wage that we define as double because it could have a decimal point. We initialize it to 0.
We need to read and process the value that the user enters. To read the input values from the user, we need to define a Scanner object.

We can create a Scanner object using the operator new, as shown in this statement. The System.in object represents the standard input stream, which by default is the keyboard. It tells the java compiler that the input will be provided through keyboard.
We prompt the user to enter the number of hours that the employee has worked.
We need to read the number of hours that the employee has worked and store it in a variable. We read the input integer by calling the nextInt() method because this input is an integer.
Note that if the user provides a non-integer number, an exception will be thrown because the input type is inconsistent with the expected data type, i.e., int.
We close the scanner as we do not want to process any input from the user in the rest of the program.

To determine whether we should pay overtime to the employee, we need to test whether the employee has worked more than the standard hours in a work week. If the employee has worked more than the standard hours in a work week, then the payment should take into account the overtime hours and we need to pay overtime at "time and a half" of the regular rate of pay. Otherwise, we pay the employee based on the number of hours that the employee has worked and the regular pay rate.

The if statement tests whether the number of hours entered by the user is greater than the standard hours in a work week. If the number of hours is greater than the standard hours in a work week, then the body of this if statement gets executed. Otherwise, the body of this if statement is skipped.

When the number of hours is greater than the standard hours in a work week, we need to pay the employee for the standard hours in a work week plus the overtime hours that the employee has worked.

The standard hours in a work week are paid at a regular pay rate. The overtime hours are paid at a rate one and a half times the regular pay rate. Therefore, the employee’s overtime rate of pay is the regular pay rate multiplied by 1.5.

If the above if test fails (i.e., when the employee has worked less than or equal to the standard hours in a work week), we should calculate the wage based on the number of hours that the employee has worked and the regular pay rate.

The statement inside the body of this else statement is executed when the if condition is false, i.e., the number of hours is less than or equal to the standard hours in a work week. Otherwise, the body of this else statement is skipped.
When there are no overtime hours, the wage is calculated based on the number of hours that the employee has worked and the regular pay rate.
We want to print the monetary value stored in variable wage using the currency formatting. To do this, we request an object from getCurrencyInstance() method.
This statement prints to the default standard output stream the text "Wage: ", and the value of the formatted variable. The printed text is followed by the end-of-line character at the end.
The expression in the argument of the println method returns a string that is obtained by concatenating the given string and value of the formatted variable.
